full_judgment:
The occurrence took place on 14-2-2002 at about 5-30/6-00 am and the FIR was lodged on 16-2-2002. In the said FIR, commission of overt acts has been alleged against almost all accused in inflicting fatal blows and causing grievous hurt with intent to commit murder by using sharp cutting weapons and in the course of this consorted attack, the witness No. 1, Harun-or-Rashid, the informant and others came forward to save the victim and themselves also received fatal injuries caused by several blows inflicted with Chinese Kural, Hashua, iron rod etc. In the result the witnesses No. 1 and 4 other witnesses were injured and the said FIR was lodged following the incident that took place on 14-2-2002. There is allegation of looting money and other valuables too. Accordingly, the aforesaid Police Station case has been registered against 25 accused persons under sections 143/448/ 323/324/325/326/ 307/380/385/387/114/34 of the Penal Code. Immediately after filing the FIR, it appears also from record that the witness No. 1, who was allegedly the target of the mob had succumbed to the injuries on 19-2-2002, while he was under treatment in Rajshahi Medical College Hospital. Pursuant to the said FIR has arisen GR No. 63 of 2002 (Singra). Police had taken up investigation, inspected the place of occurrence, recorded the deposition of witnesses under section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, seized alamats, procured injury certificates, inquest report, post mortem report etc. and having found prima facie case against the aforesaid 25 accused, the IO has submitted Charge Sheet No. 134 dated 31-5-2002 under sections 147/448/323/324/325/307/302/379/ 114/34 of the Penal Code. Thereafter the case, being ready for trial, was transmitted to the court of Sessions Judge, Natore, wherein it was numbered as Sessions Case No. 105 of 2003. Thereafter the case was transferred to the court of Additional Sessions Judge, Natore, for trial and the trial court by its order No. 50 dated 18-7-2007 has framed charge against all the accused petitioners under sections 147/448/ 323/324/325/326/307/302/379/114/34 of the Penal Code and, noticeably, an application filed under section 494 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, filed on behalf of 4 accused persons was also rejected by the same order. It further, appears that, after framing the charge out of 25 accused, the accused No. 5 and accused No. 9 have expired. It also appears from the materials on record that after framing of the charge, 24 accused petitioners filed Criminal Revision No. 1482 of 2007, challenging the charge framing order dated 18-7.2007, passed in Sessions Case No. 105 of 2003. It further transpires from the record that, on 19-11-2007, a Rule was issued in that Criminal Revision No. 1482 of 2007 and all further proceedings of Sessions Case No. 105 of 2003 was stayed for a period of 3(three) months and, thereafter, the period of stay was extended till disposal of the rule by a Bench of this Division. It is also revealed from the record that the Rule issued in Criminal Revision No. 1482 of 2007, arising out of Sessions Case No. 105 of 2003, was discharged for default by a Division Bench of this court, vide order dated 8-5-2014 passed in the said Criminal Revision No. 1482 of 2007. However, as the record shows, the concerned Public Prosecutor, thereafter, filed an application under section 494 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, on 23-7-2014, for withdrawal of the aforesaid Sessions Case No. 105 of 2003, although at a stage when process has been issued for adducing witnesses, vide order No. 71, dated 28-5-2014 of the trial court, also recording that the proceedings of the said sessions case has been resumed since the order of stay granted by the High Court Division was no more in existence. The trial court, thereafter, by the impugned judgment and order No.75 dated 26-8-2014, passed by Mr Md Rahibul Islam, the Additional Sessions Judge, Natore, in Sessions Case No. 105 of 2003, the petition filed under section 494 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, was allowed and acquitted the accused. Being aggrieved thereby, the informant has filed this petition under section 435 read with section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and obtained the present Rule.

In the decisions reported in 49 DLR (AD) 143, 2000 BLD (AD) 54 = 52 DLR (AD) 8, 1996 BLD 418 = 49 DLR 589, besides other numerous decisions of India and Pakistan, it was held that, "non-compoundable offences cannot be withdrawn and the learned Magistrate or, to that effect, the learned Sessions Judge should pass a judicial order applying his judicial mind."
